alex_dev: quick question before I merge a TF change that creates a per-tenant k8s namespace + minimal RoleBinding for our uploader service account. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/5678
maria_infra: paste the TF snippet you plan to apply? prefer namespace-scoped Role instead of ClusterRole unless there's a clear need.
alex_dev: here the snippet: ```resource "kubernetes_namespace" "tenant_ns" { metadata { name = "tenant-${var.tenant_id}" } }
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "uploader_sa" { metadata { name = "uploader" namespace = kubernetes_namespace.tenant_ns.metadata[0].name annotations = { "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.uploader.arn } } }
resource "kubernetes_role" "secrets_read" { metadata { name = "secrets-reader" namespace = kubernetes_namespace.tenant_ns.metadata[0].name } rule { api_groups = [""] resources = ["secrets"] verbs = ["get","list"] } }
resource "kubernetes_role_binding" "bind" { metadata { name = "uploader-bind" namespace = kubernetes_namespace.tenant_ns.metadata[0].name } subject { kind = "ServiceAccount" name = kubernetes_service_account.uploader_sa.metadata[0].name namespace = kubernetes_namespace.tenant_ns.metadata[0].name } role_ref { kind = "Role" name = kubernetes_role.secrets_read.metadata[0].name api_group = "rbac.authorization.k8s.io" } }```
alex_dev: security goal: only that SA can read secrets in its tenant ns. S3 access via IRSA role. Any red flags? :thinking_face:
maria_infra: couple things:
- set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on pods that don't need k8s creds.
- ensure IAM role trust policy is OIDC-based and scoped to the SA name+namespace. we have a module that generates that pattern.
- TF race: role must exist before SA annotation or EKS API rejects it.
jamie_sre: we hit that race before. pattern we use: 1) create aws_iam_role 2) attach policies 3) create k8s SA with eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn. either split into two applies or add explicit depends_on linking the SA to the IAM role resources.
alex_dev: ok I'll add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role.uploader]` and note in README about two-step apply if needed.
jamie_sre: also consider a tiny CI check that waits for IAM role propagation before applying SA in staging to reduce flakes. I can prototype a wrapper that polls STS or checks the role->webidentity provider mapping.
alex_dev: please do, I'll open a ticket and tag eng-infra.
maria_infra: secret wiring note: you said secrets are synced from SSM via a controller? If you switch to Secrets Store CSI + aws-secretsmanager-provider, remember the CSI provider needs cluster-level permissions and a constrained provider role. that can widen blast radius if not careful.
alex_dev: yep currently a per-namespace controller syncs from SSM. thinking about CSI but leaning to per-namespace controller for least privilege.
maria_infra: also, tighten Role verbs to target explicit secret names if you can predict them (e.g., resources: ["secrets/my-uploader-creds"]). least privilege.
alex_dev: good idea. in our case the secret name is deterministic: `uploader-${var.tenant_id}-creds`, so I'll scope it.
maria_infra: one more Q: do we need any namespace annotation for IAM?
jamie_sre: no, only the SA needs `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`. namespace-level annotations aren't used for IRSA. RBAC on namespace still applies.
ops-bot: deploy-check: terraform plan OK in staging for tenant-99, no k8s resources applied.
alex_dev: thanks all  plan updates: add depends_on to SA, set automountServiceAccountToken false in helm values, scope Role to specific secret name, add README note about apply ordering, open ticket for CI propagation check. will ping for final review. :thumbsup:
maria_infra: lgtm, ping when ready for review.
jamie_sre: if you want I can add the small polling step in CI repo once ticket is up.
alex_dev: opening ticket now, tagging you. thanks! :raised_hands:
